messages:
Alice M: Quick sync — we need to finalize the runtime -> infra telemetry labels for routing/quotas/dashboards. TL;DR: keep Prom labels low-cardinality, follow OTel where sensible, and add a lightweight rollouts tag for UX.
Ben P: +1. Any concrete proposal?
Carla S: I sketched something in the doc: https://docs.redwood-inference.internal/telemetry/proposal — main points: use snake_case, reserve `tenant_id` for logs only (too high-card), expose `tenant_tier` instead, and add `route_group` instead of raw route paths.
Dmitri K: Important: routing policies need `route_decision` and `fallback_reason` labels so we can count fallbacks by cause. But careful — `route` names explode. 
Alice M: Exactly. Proposal snippet:```
service: "redwood-runtime"
env: "prod|staging"
model_family: "gptx-13b"
model_variant: "q4_0|fp16"
route_group: "chat|embed|rerank"
route_decision: "primary|fallback|cache_hit"
fallback_reason: "no_capacity|latency|error"
rollout_id: "canary-2026-03"
tenant_tier: "free|team|enterprise"
```
Carla S: That looks good. Two comments: 1) `model_variant` should be enumerated in ingest rules to avoid free-form strings; 2) `rollout_id` must be optional and only present when a rollout header is present from Console.
Ben P: For latency metrics we should expose a histogram (prom summary?) with buckets tuned for target SLOs (5ms/10ms/25ms/50/100/250/500/1000). Use histogram for percentile calc, store exemplar ids for trace linking.
Dmitri K: Agree on buckets. Also: add `request_tier` to help split by dedicated vs hosted (affects capacity routing).
Alice M: Good call. Add `deployment_tier: "hosted|dedicated|private"`. We should document cardinality limits per label: <=10 values for env, <=20 for model_family, <=100 for model_variant, <=1000 for route_group? Maybe route_group should be <=50.
Carla S: Let's not hardcode numbers in Slack. Suggest table in the doc and we iterate in the metrics stewarding meeting.
infra-bot: Note: created meeting "telemetry-ontology-handoff" for 1922468400. Invitees: eng-platform, eng-runtime, eng-ml.
Ben P: One more internal API debate: do we emit two metrics: `inference_request_total{route_group,...}` and `inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{...}` or unify under `inference_request` with type label? I prefer separate metric names (counter + histogram) to keep Prom idioms.
Dmitri K: Separate is cleaner for alerting. counters for qps, histograms for latency. Add gauge `inflight_requests` with safe cardinality.
Alice M: Ok next steps: Carla will move the label table to the doc, Ben will propose histogram buckets + exemplar plan, Dmitri will draft routing label generation (how runtime maps policy->route_group). I'll own rollout_id conventions and Console header spec.
Carla S: I'll also add a migration playbook: how to backfill dashboards and a temporary shim that maps old `route` -> `route_group` for 4 weeks.
Ben P: ack. Also want to run a small cardinality probe job in staging to catch any unexpected label explosion.
Dmitri K: ping @Alice M when probe is up and I'll wire in the dashboards.
Alice M: Great. If nobody objects, I'll lock the schema PR by EOD and schedule the stewarding meeting notes. :thumbsup:
Carla S: No objections from my side.
infra-bot: Meeting created and calendar invites sent.
Ben P: thanks — will review the PR after lunch.
Alice M: Thanks all — see you at the meeting.
